prize_parts.citation: for a body of work that renews poetry, the essay and the book itself through an exacting, emotionally charged dialogue with antiquity

statement.case_for: On public knowledge, Carson has one of the most recognisable voices on the list. She joins classical scholarship, lyric, verse narrative, essay, translation and the designed book, and the invention serves what the work is about. Autobiography of Red recasts a Stesichorean fragment as a modern verse novel about desire and selfhood. Nox turns elegy for a brother into a physical object whose form is part of its mourning. In both, formal daring carries real intellectual depth and emotional force, and neither works as a mere experiment. The work spans several decades and several modes, which supports sustained quality. She writes in English, so my judgment is less mediated by translation than it is for several other candidates. I do not treat that as merit in itself; it only lowers one uncertainty. Judged by distinctiveness of voice, formal and linguistic achievement, imaginative depth and range across the oeuvre, she is my strongest candidate, and I remain with my opening first place.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is the one Olsson and Mattson raise: much of the oeuvre is hybrid, translational or tied to book design and performance. It is hard to separate her original creation from scholarship and versions of ancient texts, and hard to say which works will prove canonical. If the citation leans on genre-crossing, it risks being vague about what the achievement is. It may also read as a prize for method rather than for a few indispensable works. A related risk is that the classical allusiveness narrows the readership. I cannot independently verify the later books or how evenly the recent output is received.

responses.point: The chair ranks Cărtărescu first and Carson second. He notes that Carson's genre-crossing work may sit awkwardly with the will's wording on an 'idealistic' direction, and that her translation and classical-scholarship component is hard to separate from original creation.
responses.response: I take the delimitation problem seriously and would answer it in the citation. The credit should rest on the original books, chiefly Autobiography of Red and Nox, with the translations and versions as evidence of the same practice rather than as separate claims. On the will's wording, I read the idealistic direction as a seriousness of purpose, not a subject matter. I find that in the sustained treatment of loss, desire and the claims of the past, and in the ethical weight she gives to the labour of reading and rendering ancient texts. I agree that this needs discussion and I do not consider it settled. I also concede that Cărtărescu's case is the strongest alternative. On my reading his scale and consistency are the point, and where we differ is how much I weigh translation-dependence of the prose texture against a body of work I can assess more directly.

responses.point: Mattson ranks Cărtărescu first and Carson third. She finds Carson's originality real but her range of modes makes a single central achievement hard to define, says the weight of her canonical works is still debated, and asks how much lies in scholarship and translation rather than original work.
responses.response: The point about a missing single centre is fair, and it is the main reason I do not call this case easy. My answer is that the centre is a recurring practice rather than one book: making an inherited form carry present grief and desire, and doing so by reshaping the form itself. That recurs across the verse novel, the essay and the object-book. I would not rest the case on the scholarship or the translations. If the committee found that only a few titles carry the case, I would see that as a reason to word the citation narrowly, not to withdraw support. I accept that I cannot show that the formal experiments will endure. I can only say that the discussion around the central works suggests staying power. That discussion is itself not proof.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg ranks Carson first. He values the formal invention and emotional force, but worries that the scholarly and classical allusiveness may narrow the readership, and that the most radical books are demanding, so the case needs a body of work behind it.
responses.response: I agree that the case has to rest on the whole body of work and not on the two best-known titles. On readership, I would not make breadth of audience the test of merit. The will asks for the most outstanding work in an ideal direction, not the most widely read. Still, the concern is useful: I would want the citation to name the emotional pull of the work, and not only the classical apparatus, so that it reflects what the books do. Where I would press further is on the later and more performance-oriented books, which I cannot verify. They are where I would want a colleague with closer knowledge to test the claim of sustained quality.

responses.point: Palm ranks Carson first and Cărtărescu second. She asks whether the hybrid formats will prove lasting in the canon or remain influential mainly among peers, and whether breadth across genres is strength or diffusion.
responses.response: I read the breadth as strength where the same concern holds across the forms, and I think it does here. I cannot show that lasting canonical standing will follow, and I would not claim it. For the committee's purposes the question is the quality of the achievement now. Influence among poets is partial evidence, not proof. The risk of diffusion would be real if the later books only repeated the early devices, so I would want that tested against the later work before the vote, not assumed away.

uncertainties: Whether the hybrid, performance-linked and object-based works can be judged fairly from text and description alone.
How to separate Carson's original literary work from her translations and versions of ancient texts under the wording of Nobel's will.
Whether the quality of her later output matches the central earlier works; I cannot independently verify the recent books.
For Cărtărescu, Michon, Tawada and others, the translation fidelity and corpus coverage on which any comparison depends.
My knowledge rests on general public information, not fresh reading, and I do not claim to have verified any source.
Whether the co-opted member votes in committee is undocumented; my simulated vote is a modeling assumption.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. Her own work is biography and non-fiction, and nothing in the profile links her to any shortlisted writer. Her literary practice is context only and is not evidence of a preference.
